title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Industry Leigong Large Model
summary: Huawei and Yunnan Baiyao present the Leigong model for traditional Chinese medicine and report faster herbal sorting and lower Poria return costs; health benefits remain proposed.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Yunnan Baiyao reports that the Leigong model took second prize in the national final of the 2024 Data Elements x contest on 24 October 2024. In their submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, Huawei and Yunnan Baiyao describe a traditional Chinese medicine model that spans cultivation, production, research, and guidance. The companies associate AI applications with 30–50-fold gains in sorting efficiency and with annual Poria return costs lower by CNY 50 million. They also associate the applications with 30–50% higher patient satisfaction. The submission does not specify the measurement methods. It does not tie each result to one deployment. Health effects remain unmeasured. No independent source reports the sorting, cost or satisfaction figures.
purpose: Improve knowledge use and operational decisions across the TCM supply chain.
system: Leigong large model for traditional Chinese medicine
developer: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. and Yunnan Baiyao Group Co., Ltd.

ratings.reason: The companies report improved sorting accuracy, 30–50-fold efficiency gains and lower Poria return costs. The attribution to the system and the baseline definitions remain unclear.

The companies associate the applications with 30–50% higher patient satisfaction, but they tie the figure to no deployment, survey or method, so its extent cannot be established, and no health outcome is measured.
The companies state global acceptance of traditional medicine as an aim. No source measures a population outcome.

The Leigong submission reports faster herbal sorting, lower Poria return costs, and improved knowledge access, alongside proposed health benefits.

The account combines several applications without measurement methods for the 30–50-fold sorting gain, CNY 50 million lower returns, or satisfaction change. Its 300% accuracy-improvement claim also needs the baseline and metric. Gross savings exclude implementation costs, and satisfaction or manufacturing efficiency does not establish clinical effectiveness.

The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public record and its assessments

fields.account: Yunnan Baiyao reports that the Leigong model took second prize in the national final of the 2024 Data Elements x contest on 24 October 2024. In their submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, Huawei and Yunnan Baiyao describe a traditional Chinese medicine model that spans cultivation, production, research, and guidance. The companies associate AI applications with 30–50-fold gains in sorting efficiency and with annual Poria return costs lower by CNY 50 million. They also associate the applications with 30–50% higher patient satisfaction. The submission does not specify the measurement methods. It does not tie each result to one deployment. Health effects remain unmeasured. No independent source reports the sorting, cost or satisfaction figures.

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
